def: A repeated choice among options with unknown payouts, where each pull both earns reward and teaches you about that option.
The trade-off between trying uncertain options to learn more and repeating the option that currently looks best.
The reward lost compared with always choosing the best option, summed over all the choices made.
A bandit strategy that picks a random option with probability epsilon and the best-looking option otherwise.
A bandit rule that picks the option with the highest average reward plus an optimism bonus that is larger for rarely tried options.
A bandit strategy that samples a plausible payout rate for each option from its posterior belief and picks the highest sample.
A search that grows a tree by repeating selection, expansion, random simulation and backpropagation, then plays the most-visited move.
Upper confidence bounds applied to trees: choosing the move at every tree node with the UCB1 rule.
A fast simulation from a tree leaf to the end of the game, used to estimate how good the leaf is.
The AlphaZero selection rule, which scales the exploration bonus by the network's prior probability for each move.
A temporary pessimistic visit added to a node so that parallel search workers spread out instead of choosing the same leaf.
A system that learns games by self-play, training a policy and value network on the visit counts and results of its own tree search.
